procedure: whole DSLIB families in seeded random order until >= 15 projects; accepted when >= 6 projects are eligible under the primary label (grew: >= 30 activities and >= 5 in each class); otherwise the next seed
use: development_only() from src/frozen.py in every script that trains, tunes, calibrates, sets thresholds or compares variants
the frozen projects are read once, by the final evaluation, after every decision is fixed
limits_on_validity: The final within-project number rests on the eligible frozen projects only (see n_eligible_grew). With so few projects its confidence interval is wide; small differences cannot be claimed.
The frozen set is DSLIB only. The final number says nothing direct about projects like those of BHD (mid-execution snapshots, much higher overrun rate). BHD results are development results.
The frozen families are not untouched: they were part of E1, E2, E2b and E2c. From the freeze on, no decision may use them.
The draw was conditioned on holding >= 6 eligible projects, so the frozen set is richer in eligible projects than a plain random draw; rejected attempts are listed.
Families come from name similarity with thresholds chosen by us (E2b). Another rule would give another frozen set.
Eligibility was counted with the primary label on whole projects. Under the tolerance label fewer frozen projects are eligible (see n_eligible_tolerance).
